issues.detail: The Hebrew 'עַמִּים יְנַגַּח יַחְדָּו אַפְסֵי אָרֶץ' means 'with them he shall push the peoples together to the ends of the earth' — the Chinese '藉著這角，他必抵觸萬民，直到地的無有' renders 'עַמִּים' as '萬民' (all peoples) and 'אַפְסֵי אָרֶץ' as '地的無有' (the nothingness of the earth), which is a mistranslation of 'ends of the earth' (אַפְסֵי אָרֶץ) as '無有' (nothingness) rather than 'ends/extremities'. This changes the meaning from pushing peoples to the ends of the earth to pushing them until the earth's nothingness.

The Hebrew 'וְהֵם רִבְבוֹת אֶפְרַיִם וְהֵם אַלְפֵי מְנַשֶּׁה' means 'and they are the ten-thousands of Ephraim, and they are the thousands of Manasseh' — the Chinese '他們是以法蓮的萬軍之主，他們是瑪拿西的千軍' adds '主' (Lord) and '軍' (army) which are not in the Hebrew; the Hebrew simply says 'ten-thousands of Ephraim' and 'thousands of Manasseh' referring to the horns/people, not 'Lord of hosts' or 'armies'. This is an addition that changes the meaning.
